title: Scalar models pass through restriction isomorphisms on an extended stratification
statement:
Let $T,X,Y$ be quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $h:X\hookrightarrow T$ and $k:Y\hookrightarrow T$ be immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] with disjoint images covering $|T|$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R_W=\Lambda_W$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their module pullbacks [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Let $M$ be an $R_X$-module and $H$ an $R_T$-module, supplied with $R_X$-module and $R_Y$-module isomorphisms $h^*H\cong M$ and $k^*H\cong0$.
Let $(s_a:X_a\hookrightarrow X)_{a<n}$ be a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification]. Assume that the extended stratification has exactly $n+1$ strata, indexed with $Y$ first and the old strata following in their given order. Assume that the family $(h\circ s_a)_{a<n}$ together with $k$ is a finite stratification of $T$ with constructible locally closed images [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Fix, for each $a$, a pro-étale cover $\{v_{a,r}:V_{a,r}\to X_a\}_r$, finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_{a,r}$ and model isomorphisms $v_{a,r}^*s_a^*M\cong R_{V_{a,r}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,r}$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible].
Then $(h\circ s_a)^*H\cong s_a^*M$ for every $a$, and the same covers and scalar modules give isomorphisms $v_{a,r}^*(h\circ s_a)^*H\cong R_{V_{a,r}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,r}$. On the additional stratum $Y$, $k^*H$ has a finite constant local model on the identity cover with scalar module $0$, whose finite presentation is $\Lambda(*)^0\to\Lambda(*)^0\to0\to0$ and whose scalar extension is zero. This specified extended stratification is adapted to $H$, so $H$ is constructible in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text:
Write $\beta:h^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the supplied module isomorphism. For each $a$, evaluate the composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] at $H$, with $f=s_a$ and $g=h$, and compose with $s_a^*\beta$. This gives
$$e_a:(h\circ s_a)^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}s_a^*h^*H\xrightarrow{s_a^*\beta}s_a^*M.$$
The second arrow is an isomorphism because applying the functor $s_a^*$ to $\beta^{-1}$ gives its inverse: both composites are identities by preservation of composition and identities. Every arrow is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_{X_a}}$, so this proves the first asserted restriction isomorphism without forgetting the module actions.

proof.text:
Denote the given model isomorphism on $V_{a,r}$ by $\theta_{a,r}:v_{a,r}^*s_a^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{V_{a,r}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,r}$. Define the required model by the actual composite
$$v_{a,r}^*(h\circ s_a)^*H\xrightarrow{v_{a,r}^*e_a}v_{a,r}^*s_a^*M\xrightarrow{\theta_{a,r}}R_{V_{a,r}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,r}.$$
Its inverse is $v_{a,r}^*(e_a^{-1})\circ\theta_{a,r}^{-1}$. Thus the covers, scalar modules and their finite presentations are exactly the given ones. By clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], these are finite constant local models on every old stratum.

proof.text: The finite free module of rank zero is the empty biproduct, hence zero by the biproduct hom-extensionality principle. Compose its isomorphism with zero with the inverse of the canonical isomorphism from the cokernel of a zero morphism to its target. This supplies exactly the rank-zero presentation. The scalar-model pullback from the point preserves zero: pointUpperStar is a left adjoint and upperStarFromPoint preserves finite colimits, so its mapMod functor is additive. Apply the canonical mapZeroObject isomorphism. This is the zero case of the transport and scalar-extension functors of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

proof.text: Use the singleton identity cover $\{\mathrm{id}_Y:Y\to Y\}$: the identity is weakly étale, and each affine open covers itself, so this is a cover by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\gamma:k^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}0$ for the other supplied isomorphism. Even when restriction to the identity cover is written as the functor $F=(\mathrm{id}_Y)^*$, its value at zero is zero: the pullback adjunction $F\dashv(\mathrm{id}_Y)_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(F0,N)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(0,(\mathrm{id}_Y)_*N)$, a singleton, and the same initial-object argument as in step 3 gives $F0\cong0$. Compose $F\gamma$ with this isomorphism and the inverse of the scalar-extension isomorphism from step 3. This supplies the required finite constant local model with scalar module $0$ on the identity cover of $Y$.

old_proof.text:
Put $A=\Lambda(*)$. The zero $A$-module has the stated finite presentation $A^0\to A^0\to0\to0$: each term is zero and each image and kernel is zero. The constant sheaf $0_Y$ is the zero module sheaf, since all its sections and all its restriction maps are zero (the singleton section sets already satisfy the sheaf condition). Let $E=R_Y\otimes_{A_Y}0_Y$. The extension--restriction adjunction in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], for the scalar ring map $A_Y\to R_Y$, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R_Y}(E,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A_Y}(0_Y,\operatorname{Res}N).$$
For every $N$ the right side contains exactly the zero morphism, so $E$ is initial. Consequently the unique maps $E\to0$ and $0\to E$ are inverse: their composites are the unique endomorphisms of the two initial objects and hence their identities. This proves the scalar-extension isomorphism $R_Y\otimes_A0\cong0$ used in the zero local model.
